high.title: Busan Bank Sees Dollar-Won Overshooting Gradually Easing in H2, Forecasts 1,490 Won in Q4
high.summary:
BNK Busan Bank has published a second-half KRW outlook forecasting the dollar-won exchange rate will gradually decline, with a Q4 target of 1,490 won. The bank cites accumulating won-positive fundamentals — most notably robust semiconductor export momentum and a narrowing Korea-U.S. interest rate differential — as the primary drivers of expected KRW appreciation. However, the bank explicitly flags key risks that could delay or moderate the pace of won recovery: Middle East geopolitical tensions, the trajectory of foreign capital flows into Korean assets, and the Federal Reserve's evolving monetary policy stance.

**Market Implications:** A 1,490 target for Q4 implies meaningful KRW strength from current levels, which would be constructive for Korean government bond (KTB) investors via reduced FX hedge costs and supportive of foreign inflows into Korean equities. KRW traders should closely monitor semiconductor export data, Fed communications, and monthly foreign portfolio flow figures as leading indicators for the timing of any USD/KRW downside move. The caveat around geopolitical and capital flow risks warrants maintaining hedged positions until clearer directional signals emerge.

high.title: Falling Oil Prices Ease Inflation Pressure – Weak Dollar May Return as Fed Rate Hike Concerns Subside
high.summary:
Woori Bank economist Min Kyung-won argues that a softer dollar environment — similar to that seen in early 2026 — could re-emerge if declining international oil prices continue to alleviate U.S. inflationary pressures, thereby reducing the probability of further Fed rate hikes. For Korea specifically, the analyst highlights solid domestic economic fundamentals as an additional tailwind supporting a downward stabilization of the dollar-won rate in H2 2026.

**Market Implications:** This view reinforces the broader H2 KRW recovery narrative. Lower oil prices reduce Korea's import bill, directly improving the trade balance and current account — both structurally positive for KRW. If the Fed pivots dovish sooner than expected, the Korea-U.S. rate differential compression accelerates, providing the BOK with additional policy flexibility. KTB investors should watch U.S. CPI releases and oil price trends as key catalysts. A sustained USD weakening trend would likely trigger foreign inflows into KTBs and KOSPI, tightening spreads and supporting equity valuations.

high.title: NDF at 1,535.70/1,536.10 Won, Up 4.45 Won
high.summary: The dollar-won one-month NDF rose overnight in the New York market, last quoted at a mid-rate of 1,535.90 won. After adjusting for the one-month swap point of -0.55 won, this implies a 4.45 won gain relative to the previous Seoul spot close of 1,532.00 won. The bid/ask spread was tight at 1,535.70 / 1,536.10, suggesting orderly but directionally firm offshore demand for dollars. This NDF move is a critical leading indicator for the Seoul onshore open — a 4+ won implied gap higher signals that the domestic market is likely to open with KRW weakness. FX traders should watch whether onshore participants absorb this pressure or whether dollar buying accelerates. The move reflects residual risk-off sentiment driven by U.S. equity weakness and geopolitical uncertainty (Iran/Strait of Hormuz tensions). Watch for BOK proximity to the 1,540 level, which could trigger verbal or operational intervention signals.

high.title: Dollar-Won Pares Losses on Risk-Off Sentiment, Closes at 1,535.80 Won
high.summary: The dollar-won rate in overnight New York trading closed at 1,535.80 won as of 2:00 AM Korean time, representing a 6.90 won decline from the prior Seoul close — but importantly, the pair had pared a larger portion of its earlier losses. The reversal was triggered by a tech-led selloff in U.S. equities, which reignited risk-aversion sentiment and supported the dollar index, pulling dollar-won back up from session lows. This price action illustrates the sensitivity of KRW to U.S. equity market risk sentiment — when tech names underperform, capital flight from EM assets including Korean equities can weigh on the won. For fund managers, the combination of a weaker intraday low and a recovered close near 1,535–1,536 suggests that the near-term range is compressing around this level. A clean break above 1,540 would shift the technical bias meaningfully bearish for KRW. Geopolitical tail risks (Hormuz) add asymmetric upside risk to USD/KRW.

high.title: South Korea Bond Market Weekly Outlook: U.S.-Iran Conflict May Surprise Markets, But Downside Seen as Limited
high.summary:
South Korea's bond market is expected to open on a weak footing this week (June 29–July 3) as investors digest the implications of renewed U.S.-Iran military tensions, following President Trump's announcement via Truth Social that U.S. aircraft struck Iranian military targets. The geopolitical escalation introduces a fresh risk-off catalyst that could push domestic yields higher in the near term as investors reassess global risk appetite.

However, market analysts suggest the damage may be contained. Given the pattern of repeated diplomatic ups and downs in U.S.-Iran negotiations, many market participants are likely to interpret the latest conflict as part of an ongoing negotiation process rather than a structural breakdown — potentially limiting the duration and magnitude of any bond sell-off.

high.title: ECB Board Member Signals Further Rate Hikes to Return Inflation to 2%
high.summary: ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel, widely considered one of the central bank's most influential hawkish voices, reiterated at the Petersberg Summer Dialogue in Königswinter, Germany that the ECB will pursue additional rate hikes until inflation is brought back to the 2% medium-term target. Schnabel also flagged the risk that energy price shocks could transmit into broader, more persistent inflationary pressures — a key concern for markets pricing in the ECB's terminal rate.

medium.title: KTB Competitive Auctions Expected at 16–17 Trillion Won in Aug–Sept; Share of 2–3 Year Notes to Increase
medium.summary: Korea Treasury Bond (KTB) issuance volumes, which were meaningfully reduced in response to recent interest rate volatility, are expected to normalize gradually in Q3 2026. Competitive auction volumes in August and September are projected to rise to 16–17 trillion won (~$13.5–14.4 billion), with the composition shifting toward shorter-duration 2–3 year notes rather than ultra-long-term bonds. This shift likely reflects both issuer sensitivity to long-end yield volatility and demand signals from domestic institutional investors preferring shorter maturities in an uncertain rate environment. For KTB investors, increased supply at the short end could exert modest upward pressure on 2–3 year yields, while reduced ultra-long issuance may provide relative support to the long end of the curve. Watch the Ministry of Economy and Finance's official issuance calendar for confirmation of these volumes.

medium.title: Financial Regulators Release Next Week's Schedule – BOK Governor at BIS/ECB Forum; Monetary Policy Board Minutes Due
medium.summary: The Bank of Korea Governor will be on an overseas business trip June 29–30, attending the BIS Annual Conference and Board Meeting in Basel and the ECB Forum in Portugal — key venues for global central bank coordination and communication. Critically, on June 30 at 16:00, the BOK will release minutes from the June 11 Monetary Policy Board meeting (the non-rate-decision meeting). These minutes will be closely watched for nuanced signals on the BOK's assessment of inflation, growth risks, and the rate cut trajectory. Any dovish language or dissent could move KTB yields and KRW. Traders should prepare for potential volatility around the 16:00 release on Tuesday.

medium.title: Korea Treasury Futures Mixed Amid Oil Price Plunge - 10-Year Up 16 Ticks
medium.summary: Korean government bond futures posted a mixed session in overnight trading, with the 3-year contract flat at 103.29 while the 10-year contract gained 16 ticks to close at 107.14. The divergence suggests that the long end of the curve benefited from the sharp decline in international oil prices — a deflationary signal that reduces inflation expectations and supports duration. Foreign investors were net sellers of 27 contracts in the 3-year segment, offset by retail buying, indicating some caution at the short end where BOK policy rate expectations are more directly priced. Bond investors should note that a sustained fall in oil prices could reinforce the BOK's room to maintain or ease policy rates, supporting KTB valuations — particularly at the long end. Watch upcoming BOK communications and CPI data for confirmation of this disinflationary narrative.

medium.title: S&P Affirms US Credit Rating at 'AA+' with Stable Outlook
medium.summary: S&P reaffirmed the United States' sovereign credit rating at 'AA+' with a stable outlook, citing the resilience of the U.S. economy, sustained tariff income, and expectations for fiscal deficit stabilization over the medium term. While this is a U.S.-centric event, the stable outlook removes a near-term tail risk that had the potential to rattle global sovereign bond markets — including KTBs — through risk-off contagion and UST yield volatility. A contained U.S. fiscal risk environment is broadly supportive of EM bond demand and reduces pressure on the dollar from safe-haven flows, which is marginally constructive for KRW stability. Fund managers should note that any future negative rating action on the U.S. would have outsized spillover effects on Korean assets.

medium.title: Retail Investors the Only Hope — Margin Debt Hits Record 38.6 Trillion Won, Sideline Cash at All-Time High of 136.6 Trillion Won
medium.summary:
Investor deposits (sideline cash) in Korean brokerage accounts reached 136.6 trillion won ($115.4 billion) as of June 24, nearing the all-time high of 139.7 trillion won, as foreign investors and the National Pension Service (NPS) continue net selling concentrated in the semiconductor sector. This creates an unusual market dynamic where retail investors holding record levels of dry powder have become the primary marginal buyer — and a critical swing variable for Korean equity direction. The simultaneous record in margin debt (38.6 trillion won) signals elevated leverage among retail participants, which could amplify downside volatility if sentiment shifts. For KRW traders, the persistence of large domestic cash hoards on the sidelines may act as a mild stabilizer for the won, as potential equity re-engagement would absorb domestic liquidity rather than driving capital outflows. Foreign net selling pressure, however, remains a headwind for both KOSPI and KRW.

medium.title: US-Iran Military Escalation: Airstrikes Continue as Iran Attacks Commercial Vessels in Strait of Hormuz
medium.summary: US President Trump issued an existential warning to Iran after US Central Command conducted additional airstrikes on Iranian missile, drone storage, and coastal radar facilities following continued Iranian attacks on commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a critical global oil transit chokepoint. The trigger was Iran's suicide drone strike on the commercial vessel *Ever Lovely* despite a prior ceasefire opportunity. For KRW traders, this carries indirect but meaningful risk: sustained Middle East escalation historically drives oil price spikes (Korea imports ~70% of crude), widening Korea's trade deficit and pressuring the current account. A deteriorating current account is a structural negative for KRW. Additionally, geopolitical risk-off sentiment typically triggers foreign equity outflows from emerging markets including Korea (KOSPI), adding further KRW depreciation pressure. Bond markets may see a flight-to-quality bid in US Treasuries, pulling Korean government bond yields in a complex direction — domestic risk-off could support KGBs, but imported inflation from higher oil would argue against aggressive BOK easing. Watch oil futures and USD/KRW closely.

medium.title: US Military Conducts Additional Airstrikes on Iran After Ceasefire Violations (Comprehensive)
medium.summary: This is a more detailed follow-up to the initial US-Iran airstrike report, confirming that US Central Command struck multiple Iranian targets after Iran launched further drone attacks on commercial shipping following an initial round of US strikes on the vessel *Ever Lovely* incident. The escalatory cycle — US strikes, Iranian retaliation, further US strikes — suggests the conflict is not de-escalating quickly. For Korean markets, the compounding risk is a prolonged disruption to Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes, through which a significant portion of Korea's energy imports transit. Sustained closure or major disruption would be a material macro shock for Korea's import bill and inflation outlook, complicating the BOK's rate path assessment. KRW could face meaningful selling pressure in a prolonged scenario, particularly if global risk appetite deteriorates sharply.

medium.title: Consumer Lending Hits 13.1 Trillion Won as Bank Regulations Drive Credit and Secured Loan Growth
medium.summary: Outstanding loans at consumer finance companies rose in H2 last year, driven by major lenders expanding personal credit and secured lending. Regulatory data from the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) indicates that tightening household lending rules at commercial banks is displacing borrowers into secondary and tertiary financial institutions — a classic regulatory arbitrage dynamic. For macro and rates traders, this is relevant as it signals that BOK/FSS tightening measures on bank lending are not fully suppressing household credit demand, merely redistributing it. This has implications for systemic financial stability risk and could influence the BOK's assessment of whether current monetary conditions are sufficiently restrictive. If household debt continues rising through non-bank channels, the BOK may be more cautious about cutting rates aggressively, even amid growth pressures.

medium.title: KOSPI Plunge Attributed to Semi-Annual Rebalancing — 20-Day Moving Average Seen as Near-Term Support
medium.summary:
Meritz Securities analyst Hwang Soo-wook argues that last week's sharp KOSPI selloff was primarily a technical, calendar-driven event — specifically foreign portfolio rebalancing ahead of the semi-annual closing, with June 26 representing the last effective trading day for foreigners given T+2 settlement. The analyst identifies a near-term support range of 8,050–8,450 points, with the 20-day moving average as a key technical floor to watch. For KRW traders, the distinction matters: if the equity weakness was rebalancing-driven rather than fundamentally motivated, the associated FX selling pressure on KRW may prove temporary. However, sustained foreign equity outflows — even if technical — can weigh on KRW/USD in the short term, and the resumption of foreign buying post-rebalancing would be a positive signal for both KOSPI and KRW stabilization.
